text:
Ana: Quick sprint summary — hybrid microcache + adaptive batching experiment finished. TL;DR: p50 down ~18ms, p99 down ~12%, cost per token down ~9%. :tada:
Oliver: Nice! Can you drop the benchmark links and what traffic mix this used?
Ana: Sure — test harness: internal/bench/hlc-hybrid-2026 (link) against canary traffic (10% of prod) for 48h. Mix: 60% short-chat (<=64 tokens), 30% medium (64-512), 10% long (>512).
Lee: Where did most of the win come from? batching or cache changes?
Ana: Split roughly 55/45. Biggest single lift was reducing KV cache miss amplification on short-chained conversations — reduced redundant KV evictions by ~40%. Adaptive microbatcher improvements shaved scheduling overhead for short requests.
Maria: Any regressions observed? latency tails for long requests?
Ana: No significant regression in end-to-end p99 for long requests in canary; small p75 bump (~6ms) but overall cost improved. We measured hallucination/regression via eval set — no drop in quality above noise.
Tara: What config flips did you use? Need code snippet to copy to Dedicated config.
Ana: Flip is behind two feature flags: hybrid_microcache_v2 and adaptive_microbatch_v3. Example deploy config we used:
```
runtime:
  feature_flags:
    hybrid_microcache_v2: true
    adaptive_microbatch_v3: true
  routing:
    short_req_threshold: 64
    prefetch_pool_size: 128
```
Anita: Can you annotate the rollout playbook? I want steps before we flip to 50%/100% — include rollback thresholds.
Ana: Added playbook to the doc, excerpt: monitor token/s and p99 per-pool, abort if p99 increases >15% for 30m or error-rate >0.2%. Automatic rollback is configured in canary controller.
Deploy-bot: Canary deployment started for experiment/hlc-hybrid-2265 at 2265432115 — 10% traffic.
Oliver: Any manual testing on Dedicated nodes with reserved capacity? Sometimes autoscaler interactions differ.
Ana: Yes — ran a 6h soak on a 16-GPU Dedicated pool with reserved slots; results matched hosted canary within 3% variance. Notes in doc.
Maria: Cost math for Finance: how did you compute the 9% per-token improvement?
Ana: We compared token billed CPU/GPU seconds across matched request samples, normalized by token count and model variant. Calculation steps in bench doc appendix.
Tara: Recommend we add a short internal announcement for customers on Dedicated rollout schedule. I'll draft.
Anita: I want a quick runbook for oncall if something goes wrong — include alert dashboards + playbook link.
Ana: Added alert set: prefetched_kv_miss_rate, microbatch_queue_depth, p99_latency_by_route. Playbook link included.
Oliver: Cool — can we target 50% traffic by EOD tomorrow if no regressions?
Ana: Yes, plan: 10% -> 25% at +3h -> 50% at +18h if metrics stable. I'll post status updates in this thread during rollout.
Maria: :thumbsup: thanks for the thorough work.
Tara: Drafted customer note and pinged product for review.
Ana: Final note: performance knobs we touched are low-risk, but we still need to watch regional variance. Plan to enable global only after regional 50% passes.
Deploy-bot: Canary update at 2265432170 — traffic increased to 25%.
Ana: Rolling checks now, will post final numbers after 24h of 25% run. :eyes:
